reviewSummary: The subject records what the bytes say and nothing more. The dual ACCEPT it records is real and the two Stage A shapes are recited without being crossed: Claude's ACCEPT is a top-level verdict with no decision field, no blockers field and no count fields, carrying six observationsNotFindings objects OBS-1 through OBS-6 with member set [id, observation]; Codex's ACCEPT carries a decision string, empty blockers and observations lists, and numeric zero counts. The six findings frozen against g19 leftover-join.v9 - four labelled Claude identifiers and two unlabeled Codex findings - are named as named and unlabeled as unlabeled, with no identifier invented for either Codex finding. The one substantive movement in this entry, OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING going stale as an authoring claim on DR-G19, is exactly the condition D-332 named as outstanding and D-333 discharged on DR-124, and it is corroborated against the candidate's own obligation bits rather than accepted on assertion. Nothing is stolen from DR-124: state-class leftover-join.v5 still measures its three leftovers on disk. No row is SATISFIED, file 08 and COORD are byte-identical, required-now stays 28, DR-G19 stays OPEN, v9 stays unrecorded and v8's currency is qualified everywhere it appears. Zero MUST-FIX and zero SHOULD-FIX.
residualObservationsNotCharged: Six tokens in the subject carry a stray space inside the lineage name - 'g19-leftover- join.v10.json' at line 7 and 'leftover- join' in the disclaimers at lines 20, 21, 28, 30 and 31 - and the line-7 token sits inside backticks, so as written it names no file on disk. Not charged: the authoritative pins are elsewhere and correct - the Subject limb cites docs/coop/artifacts/g19-leftover-join.v10.json and the Stage A table cites both review paths, all with digests I recomputed and matched - and the identical spacing is already live in the adopted D-333 COORD entry, where it occurs sixteen times, so it is transcription style rather than a claim about bytes. Worth repairing at transcription; not a defect in the record.

There is no blank line between the closing blockquote line 42 and 'D-333 is ADOPTED at' on line 43, so lines 43-46 render as lazy continuation of the disclaimer blockquote, and line 46 is unwrapped where the rest of the preamble wraps near column 72. Not charged: the adopted D-333 draft has the identical break and wrapping, and no recorded fact changes.

D-332 carried 'Does not remasure g19-fixture-corpus.v3' and 'Does not close leftover-design of OBL-G19-FX-AUTHORING'; the subject drops both. Not charged: dropping the second is required, because this entry does remasure that leftover stale on DR-G19, and dropping the first asserts nothing false - g19-fixture-corpus.v3 re-hashes unmoved among the 55 verified recorded inputs and the subject does not touch it.

The 'Does not remasure' list names G20, G21, G30, SARIF and anti-lockstep leftover-join.v6 but omits g29 leftover-join.v6 (D-320) and sdk leftover-join.v9 (D-329), which are also current members. Not charged: the list makes no exhaustiveness claim, adopted siblings D-332 and D-333 carry the identical scope, and the omission asserts nothing false about either lineage.

Both the v9 and the v10 Claude Stage A reviews label their observations OBS-1 through OBS-6, and line 65 names both sets in adjacent sentences. Not charged: each sentence names the artifact version it belongs to, the disposition table scopes its row to g19 leftover-join.v10 explicitly, and I confirmed against both frozen reviews that each really does carry OBS-1 through OBS-6 with member set [id, observation], so neither recital is false and no reader can cross them.

The Decision-type limb summarises the dual ACCEPT as '(0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX)' while the disposition table records that the Claude review has no blockers field at all. Not charged: the table supplies the unflattened shape in the same document, the parenthetical is a grade summary rather than a field recital, and the identical construction was adopted at D-326 through D-331.
